summary: Samuel Johnson worked in linguistics and other fields. He studied at King Edward VI School, King Edward VI College, Stourbridge (around 1725–1726), and Pembroke College, Oxford (1728–1731).

Samuel M. Grupper specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at Indiana University Bloomington, studying under teachers Irving Yucheng Lo and Philip West (both attested 1980).
Samuel Mateer was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Bedford Theological College around 1858–1859 and served as a missionary for the London Missionary Society from 1859 to 1891.

Samuel Ross Winans worked in linguistics and Indology. After earning his A.B. at Princeton University (around 1870–1874), he served there as Professor of Greek and Instructor of Sanskrit (1876–1883) and dean of the faculty (1899–1903).

Indologist Samuel Slater studied at King's College London (~1843–1845). He served as Rector at St. Paul's School, Darjeeling (1850), Professor at Bishop's College, Calcutta (1850–1863), Professor of Hindustani at King's College London (1861–1862), and headmaster at Bishop Cotton School (1863–1886).
Samuel Swinton Jacob was a scholar in history and archaeology. He was educated at Cheam School and trained as an engineer at Addiscombe Military Seminary around 1856–1858.
Samuel Tickell worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at Addiscombe Military Seminary from 1827 to 1829 and served in the Bengal Army from around 1829 to 1865.
Samuel Wells Williams worked in Sinology and linguistics. He studied at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (~1831–1832) and held a post at Yale University from around 1877 to 1884.

Samuel William Fallon specialized in linguistics and Indology. He earned a Ph.D. from the University of Halle by 1862 and served as an inspector of schools for the Bengal Education Department from around 1857 to 1878.

Sandamali Udeshika Dissanayaka works in Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Sri Jayewardenepura (BA, 2017–2021) and the University of Kelaniya (MA, 2023–2024), and became a Temporary Lecturer at the University of Ruhuna in 2024.

Indology and religious studies scholar Sandeep Namdev Dhikale earned an M.A. at Savitribai Phule Pune University. His posts include Assistant Professor at Fergusson College (2018–2019) and MIT World Peace University (2019–2020), Research Associate (2018–2019), and JRF+SRF at SARTHI (2020–2022).
Sandford Arnot worked in Indology and linguistics. In 1826, he succeeded John Borthwick Gilchrist and served as a teacher of Hindustani at the Oriental Institution, Leicester Square.

Sandford Arthur Strong worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at King's College London, under Cecil Bendall (1881), at St John's College (1881–1890), and Oxford (1885). He held posts at Cambridge (~1894–1903) and University College London (1895).

Sandra A. Wawrytko is a scholar of philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. She taught Michael J. Tetreault and held posts at San Diego State University as Professor (attested 1999) and Associate Professor of Philosophy (attested 2014).
Sandra Bell is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. She completed her doctoral thesis at Durham University by 1991 and served as a Professor there in 1991.

Sandra Hochwarter is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned a Mag.phil. at the University of Vienna, where she studied under teacher Anne MacDonald and MA supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes.
Sandra Smets is an Indologist who completed her doctoral studies under the supervision of Christophe Vielle. She held an attested post at Université catholique de Louvain in 2004.

Sang-Kyun Sun works in Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Delhi under doctoral supervisor Sanghasen Singh (attested 1995) and held a post as Lecturer at JinGak Buddhist College (attested 1995).

Sanga Tenzin specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a BSc from Navodaya Education Trust (2012–2016), worked as a Clinical Nurse (2018), and is attested in 2026 as HoD and Assistant Professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Sangay Dorji works in Tibetology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Tengtho Monastery and Semtokha Rigney School, he taught Gembo Dorji, served as Secretary at Dzongkha Development Commission (attested 1999–2004), and became a Specialist at the Ministry of Education (2022).
